status_note: Values come from section D ('Simulation parameters for the backend engineer') of research_notes/Lunar Rover Interaction Protocol/01_positioning_and_time.md (11 Nov 2026). Source keys in square brackets and the tags MOON / MARS / EARTH / SIM / REQ / CALC are that note's; 'A' is that note's mark for an assumption anchored on its sources but not measured. Parameters listed under not_in_note_01 are not in the note's table: they are the task's values or B-96 assumptions and have no opened external source.

uwb_range_noise_m.source: note 01 D: 'UWB two-way range error, line of sight' [PLANS18, NUCH24] EARTH
uwb_range_noise_m.meaning: white noise of one short-range (UWB) two-way range

uwb_range_max_m.source: note 01 D: 'UWB maximum range', A (no lunar value is public; vendor claim of 290 m UNVERIFIED)
uwb_range_max_m.meaning: up to this true distance the range comes from the UWB radio

long_range_noise_m.source: note 01 D: 'Long-range two-way ranging over the base radio (S-band or cellular)', A
long_range_noise_m.meaning: white noise of one long-range two-way range, used beyond the UWB range

long_range_cap_m.source: note 01 D gives the limit as 'radio line of sight from existing notes'; here: the smooth-Moon mutual horizon sqrt(2 R h_a) + sqrt(2 R h_b), R = 1,737.4 km (research_notes/Lunar ATC/vehicles_comms_internals.md section 2.5, Computed), with the trace's antenna heights, and at most this cap = the engine's radio range d_max (lunarsim/atc/radio.py, provisional B-70). Terrain blocking is not modelled.
long_range_cap_m.meaning: beyond the limit A neither ranges to B nor hears its reports

nlos_bias_m.unit: m, positive, constant during a burst
nlos_bias_m.source: note 01 D: 'Range bias when the direct path is blocked', A
nlos_bias_m.meaning: range bias while the direct path is blocked

lq_detect_prob.meaning: the ranging radio's link-quality flag says degraded during a burst

lq_false_prob.meaning: the flag says degraded in line of sight

dr_error_frac.unit: 1-sigma per axis, fraction of distance driven since the last fix
dr_error_frac.source: note 01 D: 'Dead-reckoning drift, firm level ground, VO + star tracker' [MAIM07] EARTH; [DAF23, ATHA24] REQ
dr_error_frac.meaning: dead-reckoning error growth (a scale-factor error and a heading error, each constant between fixes)

dr_error_frac_loose_no_vo.source: note 01 D: 'Dead-reckoning drift, loose soil or slope above 10 deg, no VO' [HELM06] EARTH
dr_error_frac_loose_no_vo.meaning: not used in distribution; the out-of-distribution set uses 0.05, the low end of this range

fix_sigma_m.unit: m, 1-sigma; read here as per axis (the note says horizontal)
fix_sigma_m.source: note 01 D: 'Absolute fix accuracy, terrain matching, sunlit' [DAF23] REQ (5 m at 3-sigma); lower end [NASH24] MARS
fix_sigma_m.meaning: position error right after an absolute terrain fix; the dark value (3 m, [ATHA24]) is not simulated

fix_spacing_m.unit: m of driving, mean (Poisson in distance)
fix_spacing_m.source: note 01 D: 'Distance between terrain-fix opportunities, sunlit highlands', A
fix_spacing_m.meaning: absolute fixes while driving; a fix is also taken at every stop. The 120 s stop the note gives for one fix is not in the traces and is not modelled

report_noise_m.meaning: white noise on each broadcast position report, on top of the sender's navigation error

ood.note: out-of-distribution test set: the true errors change, the values A's filter assumes (above) do not
ood.source: LEAD, task B-96; 0.05 is the low end of note 01 D's loose-soil range, 2 x 0.3 m and 2 x 3 m are inside its ranging sweeps
